    df_t = df.T

    adata = ad.AnnData(
        X=df_t.values,
        obs=pd.DataFrame(index=df_t.index),

    Apply standard QC:
    - Filter cells with < MIN_GENES_PER_CELL detected genes.
    - Filter genes detected in < MIN_CELLS_PER_GENE cells.
    - Compute pct_counts_mt for mitochondrial genes.
    - Flag cells with > MAX_MT_PCT mitochondrial counts.

        adata,
        qc_vars=["mt"],
        prefix="pct_counts_",
        inplace=True,
    )

    n_cells_before = adata.n_obs
    adata = adata[adata.obs["n_genes"] >= MIN_GENES_PER_CELL].copy()

        "Cell filter: %d -> %d cells (removed %d with < %d genes)",
        n_cells_before,
        adata.n_obs,
        n_cells_before - adata.n_obs,
        MIN_GENES_PER_CELL,

        n_genes_before - adata.n_vars,

    logger.info("Flagged %d cells with > %.1f%% mitochondrial counts", n_high_mt, MAX_MT_PCT)

    and identify top N_HVG highly variable genes.

    """
    Run PCA, build neighborhood graph, compute UMAP, and perform Leiden clustering.
    """
    # PCA on highly variable genes
    logger.info("Running PCA on %d highly variable genes...", N_HVG)
    sc.pp.pca(adata, n_comps=N_PCS, use_hvg=True)

    logger.info("Building neighborhood graph with %d neighbors...", N_NEIGHBORS)
    sc.pp.neighbors(adata, n_neighbors=N_NEIGHBORS, n_pcs=N_PCS)

## Mechanism

The therapeutic efficacy of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors in *BRCA1/2*-deficient malignancies is predicated on the concept of synthetic lethality, wherein the simultaneous disruption of two non-essential pathways becomes lethal to the cell. Under normal physiological conditions, PARP1 and PARP2 are rapidly recruited to sites of DNA single-strand breaks (SSBs), where they catalyze the synthesis of poly(ADP-ribose) chains on themselves and nearby proteins. This modification serves as a scaffold for the recruitment of repair factors, including the XRCC1-LIG3 complex, facilitating the rapid repair of SSBs. When PARP enzymes are inhibited, SSBs persist and are converted into double-strand breaks (DSBs) during DNA replication. In wild-type cells, these DSBs are efficiently repaired via the homologous recombination (HR) pathway, a process critically dependent on the tumor suppressors BRCA1 and BRCA2. BRCA2, in particular, is essential for loading the RAD51 recombinase onto resected single-stranded DNA, enabling strand invasion and error-free repair.

In *BRCA1/2*-deficient cells, the HR pathway is compromised, rendering the cell unable to repair replication-induced DSBs. Consequently, the cell relies on error-prone alternative pathways, such as non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) or microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ), leading to genomic instability and cell death. A critical nuance in this mechanism is "PARP trapping." Modern PARP inhibitors, such as olaparib and rucaparib, do not merely block the catalytic activity of PARP; they trap the enzyme on damaged DNA.
